# Systems Publish Runtime Lifecycle Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `final-approved`
- Updated: `2026-07-29T11:51:52Z`

## Objective

Consolidate system deployment and runtime controls into Publish with intent-driven retained state and automatic qualified system launch, replacing the standalone Run & Test experience.

## Discovery

The completed general Run & Test roadmap introduced an application-owned capability catalog and shared workflow shell, but the resulting user experience still exposes deployment internals and its current Start action records an immediate bookkeeping handoff rather than a persistent openable system. Publish already owns recognizable builds and immutable releases. The successor should retain the reusable application foundations, correlate lifecycle state to each active published build, replace manual identifiers with intent commands, introduce a truthful long-lived runtime session, automatically launch qualified visual systems, start nonvisual servers without an Open control, and remove the standalone Run & Test surface. The earlier active-source eligibility proposal is absorbed into the same Publish correlation and lifecycle boundary.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: The successor changes deployment authority, retained operational state, runtime lifetime, exact-release rendering, automatic host launch, workspace isolation, audit history, and UI-to-host trust boundaries.
- Protected assets:
  - Workspace-owned active systems, builds, exact approved releases, and lifecycle authority
  - Deployment, runtime-session, health, execution, and audit integrity
  - Host process isolation and trusted declarative system UI
  - Authorization, policy-derived capability, secret-reference, egress, and quota decisions
  - Private system content, runtime diagnostics, conversation data, and artifact references
- Trust boundaries:
  - Publish shared UI to desktop IPC or authenticated server API
  - Application lifecycle orchestration to deployment and runtime-session repositories
  - Application runtime authority to host-composed runtime adapters
  - Verified immutable release content to the trusted declarative renderer
  - Application-issued launch descriptor to a desktop window or thin-client runtime surface
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A forged deployment, run, release, workspace, or host-target identifier controls another system
  - Duplicate, racing, stale, or reordered intents create multiple current deployments or impossible state
  - An archived, deleted, cross-workspace, mismatched, or superseded release remains operable
  - Imported or authored executable content reaches a trusted runtime or host launch surface without sandbox qualification
  - A visual runtime surface receives Node, filesystem, unrestricted network, or host-process authority
  - Partial install, activation, launch, stop, persistence, or adapter failure produces false state or hides required recovery actions
  - Raw adapter failures or runtime content leak credentials, paths, provider payloads, private data, or exploitable details
- Controls:
  - Application-owned intent use cases derive internal identifiers and eligible actions from authoritative workspace-scoped state
  - Exact-release verification, active-owner checks, optimistic concurrency, idempotency keys, finite transitions, and one-current-deployment reconciliation fail closed
  - Retained transitions and audit records preserve recovery evidence; uninstall never erases immutable or operational history
  - Only qualified trusted declarative releases produce bounded launch descriptors; unsupported executable content is denied
  - Host-owned runtime surfaces use least privilege, strict context isolation, no renderer host authority, bounded messaging, and allowlisted resources
  - Policy-derived capabilities, secret references, egress, quotas, and authorization remain outside renderer input
  - Bounded safe diagnostics and explicit partial-failure states prevent disclosure and misleading success
- Verification:
  - Transition, race, idempotency, stale-state, cross-workspace, forged-identity, partial-failure, and restart-recovery tests
  - Structured, SQLite, and PostgreSQL repository conformance for retained deployment and session state
  - Runtime adapter and declarative renderer tests for visual, nonvisual, unsupported, and failing releases
  - IPC, API, preload, client, authorization, safe-diagnostic, and host-composition parity tests
  - Packaged desktop and thin-client end-to-end qualification of automatic launch, Stop-only running state, recovery, and archive/delete exclusion
  - Architecture, documentation, agent-support, security, build, and full repository completion gates
- Residual risks:
  - Imported or authored executable systems remain unavailable until an independently qualified sandbox exists.
  - The trusted local reference runtime is not remote production orchestration; public ingress, multi-node scheduling, autoscaling, and managed deployment remain outside this successor.
  - Automated host checks do not replace production capacity, physical assistive-technology, or managed-environment qualification.

### Constraints

- Preserve the two completed general-workflow increments and reuse their application-owned catalog, handler, transport, and bounded presentation foundations where they remain appropriate.
- Published build cards, not renderer-entered deployment or run identifiers, own normal lifecycle interaction.
- Install performs install-and-activate; an activation failure must retain truthful installed state and recoverable actions rather than silently rolling back or reporting success.
- Any stopped installed system may be uninstalled. Active stopped installations expose Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall; inactive stopped installations expose Activate and Uninstall; running installations expose Stop only.
- Start automatically opens qualified visual systems in a host-owned isolated runtime surface and starts nonvisual servers without any Open System control.
- Every lifecycle command re-resolves workspace, active owning system, exact approved release, host target, current deployment, session state, authorization, and supported runtime capability.
- Immutable builds, releases, revisions, historical deployments, sessions, runs, and audit evidence are retained; uninstall is a lifecycle transition, not destructive history deletion.
- Imported or authored executable content remains unavailable until a qualified sandbox and controlled-environment evidence exist.
- The standalone Run & Test navigation, manual deployment identifier, requested-capability, secret-reference, egress-origin, and generic review forms are removed after Publish reaches feature parity.
- Use focused tests for internal chunks and run full repository gates only once after all chunks in each approved successor increment are complete.

## High-level decisions

### Published system lifecycle model

How should Publish expose install, activation, execution, launch, stop, and uninstall without asking users to manage deployment internals?

Publish consolidation is user-directed. The lifecycle must preserve exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, truthful retained state, audit history, and secure runtime authority while presenting only actions that are valid for the current system state.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `retained-stateful-lifecycle`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intent-driven retained lifecycle (retained-stateful-lifecycle) | Retain one application-owned current deployment per release and host target. Install also activates. Stopped systems expose only state-valid Start, Activate or Deactivate, and Uninstall controls; running systems expose only Stop. Start automatically opens a qualified visual system and starts a nonvisual server without an Open System control. | yes | Provides the complete user outcome but requires coordinated contract, application, persistence, runtime-session, host, transport, shared-UI, release-rendering, and documentation changes; Preserves audit, rollback, exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, and truthful lifecycle state; Requires explicit handling for partial install-and-activate failure and for a runtime that starts successfully when automatic visual launch fails | Not installed exposes Install; Install performs install then activation without exposing a separate initial Activate step; Installed, active, and stopped exposes Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall; installed, inactive, and stopped exposes Activate and Uninstall; Running exposes Stop only; Stop returns the system to its installed activation state and eligible stopped controls; Uninstall is available for any stopped installed system and records an auditable retained transition instead of deleting history; Opaque deployment and run identifiers remain internal, duplicate install intents are idempotent, and the standalone Run & Test tab is removed; Qualified built-in visual systems open automatically from verified exact-release declarative content and typed runtime bindings; nonvisual servers start without an Open control; imported or authored execution remains unavailable without a qualified sandbox |
| Existing command facade (existing-command-facade) | Move the existing operations into Publish, automatically select identifiers, and keep the current install, activate, and zero-output run semantics. | no | Smaller and faster interface change; Avoids new persistence and runtime-session contracts; Does not launch the created system or provide meaningful Start and Stop behavior | The interface becomes simpler but continues to overstate runtime functionality; Uninstall and deactivate remain aliases or unsupported; A visual system still cannot open after Start |

## Increment 1: Truthful retained lifecycle and release-bound runtime

- Id: `published-lifecycle-runtime-foundation`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Replace bookkeeping-only deployment runs with an application-owned retained lifecycle, idempotent current-deployment projection, and long-lived release-bound runtime session that supports install-and-activate, activate or deactivate, start or stop, stopped-state uninstall, and qualified visual launch.

### Work packages

- **Intent lifecycle and eligibility projection** (`lifecycle-contracts-and-orchestration`): Versioned contracts and application use cases expose authoritative state, state-valid actions, and intent commands without accepting renderer-supplied deployment or run authority.
- **Idempotent retained persistence** (`retained-persistence-and-recovery`): One current deployment per exact release and host target is reconciled from retained records; install, activation, deactivation, stop, and uninstall transitions remain auditable, retryable, and truthful across partial failures and restarts.
- **Release-bound runtime and launch descriptor** (`release-runtime-and-launch-boundary`): A long-lived runtime session starts and stops trusted exact-release systems, distinguishes visual and nonvisual releases, produces a bounded host-owned launch descriptor for qualified visual systems, and fails closed for unsupported executable content.
- **Host and transport parity** (`host-transport-security-parity`): Desktop IPC and authenticated server API expose identical workspace-scoped lifecycle behavior with sanitized failures, bounded status projections, exact-release checks, and no client-controlled internal identifiers.

### Deliverables

- Versioned lifecycle state, action-eligibility, intent, result, and launch-descriptor contracts
- Application orchestration for install-and-activate, activate, deactivate, start, stop, and stopped-state uninstall
- Idempotent retained deployment and runtime-session repositories with compatibility handling for existing records
- Trusted exact-release visual renderer and nonvisual server runtime boundaries
- Desktop and server composition plus IPC, API, preload, and client parity
- Focused state-machine, repository-conformance, isolation, denial, partial-failure, restart-recovery, and runtime tests
- Updated lifecycle, build/release, runtime, security, and host architecture documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lifecycle-transition-matrix`: The application-owned transition matrix implements Install as install-and-activate; permits Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall for an active stopped installation; permits Activate and Uninstall for an inactive stopped installation; exposes Stop as the only running action; and rejects stale or invalid transitions without side effects. | local | passed (test) |
| `idempotent-retained-state`: Repeated intents reconcile to one workspace-scoped current deployment per exact release and host target while preserving immutable release identity, audit history, prior deployments, uninstall history, and restart recovery without destructive deletion. | local | passed (test) |
| `release-bound-runtime`: Start creates a truthful long-lived runtime session bound to the selected active system and exact approved release; qualified visual releases receive a bounded launch descriptor, nonvisual releases start without one, and unsupported imported or authored execution fails closed. | local | passed (test) |
| `partial-failure-truthfulness`: Activation, automatic visual launch, stop, deactivation, uninstall, adapter, and persistence failures leave a recoverable authoritative state, expose only valid retry or cleanup actions, and never report a system as running, stopped, active, or uninstalled contrary to retained evidence. | local | passed (test) |
| `lifecycle-host-parity`: Desktop and server hosts enforce identical exact-release, workspace, authorization, state-transition, and action-eligibility semantics through allowlisted IPC and API projections with safe diagnostics. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-lifecycle-reviewed`: Workspace isolation, exact-release integrity, runtime authority, launch isolation, fail-closed unsupported execution, transition races, idempotency, audit retention, sanitized diagnostics, secure rollback, and residual risk are documented and evidenced with denial and failure-path tests. | local | passed (review) |
| `lifecycle-foundation-gates`: Focused contract, use-case, persistence, runtime, host, transport, and recovery tests pass before the applicable documentation, architecture, server/thin-client build, security, and full repository gates run once for the completed increment. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused transition-matrix tests for valid, stale, duplicate, racing, and invalid lifecycle intents.
- Run shared repository conformance against structured, SQLite, and PostgreSQL adapters for current-deployment uniqueness, retained history, uninstall, and restart recovery.
- Run focused runtime and launch tests for trusted visual releases, nonvisual servers, unsupported authored/imported content, launch failure, stop failure, and adapter loss.
- Run focused IPC, API, preload, client, host-composition, cross-workspace, forged-identity, malformed-input, and sanitized-diagnostic tests.
- After every planned chunk is complete, run applicable docs, architecture, agent-support, security, server/thin-client build, and npm test gates once for increment 1.

### Rollback

Disable the new intent handlers and launch boundary while retaining all newly written deployment, session, and audit records; fall back to a read-only unavailable state rather than restoring identifier-driven or bookkeeping-only execution paths.

### Excluded

- Arbitrary imported or authored code execution before a qualified sandbox exists
- Remote cluster scheduling, multi-node orchestration, autoscaling, and public ingress provisioning
- Deleting immutable builds, releases, revisions, deployment history, runtime-session history, or audit evidence
- Replacing domain-specific conversation, data, review, or execution authorization with renderer-owned workflow metadata

## Increment 2: Unified Publish lifecycle and automatic system launch

- Id: `publish-lifecycle-experience`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `published-lifecycle-runtime-foundation`

Make each recognizable active published build the single place to install, operate, automatically launch, stop, deactivate or reactivate, and uninstall its system while removing the standalone Run & Test tab and all manual deployment internals.

### Work packages

- **State-aware published build controls** (`published-build-lifecycle-cards`): Publish correlates system name, build version, exact release, lifecycle state, health, and the next valid actions on one build card, with duplicate submissions guarded and invalid controls absent.
- **Automatic host-native visual launch** (`automatic-host-launch`): Start automatically opens qualified visual systems in a dedicated host-owned runtime surface, starts nonvisual servers without navigation, and keeps Stop as the only running-state control.
- **Run & Test retirement** (`run-test-cutover`): The standalone tab, manual deployment identifier, requested-capability, secret-reference, egress-origin, and generic review forms are removed from the Systems navigation while reusable application-owned workflow foundations remain behind bounded lifecycle orchestration where appropriate.
- **Cross-host qualification and guidance** (`qualification-and-guidance`): Shared interaction, accessibility, packaged-desktop, thin-client, lifecycle, automatic-launch, archive/delete exclusion, and recovery tests prove the simplified end-to-end experience and canonical documentation describes it.

### Deliverables

- Responsive accessible published-build lifecycle cards and progress/status feedback
- Exact action progression for Install, Start or Stop, Activate or Deactivate, and Uninstall with no visible Open System control
- Automatic qualified visual launch in host-owned runtime surfaces and nonvisual server start behavior
- Removal of the standalone Run & Test tab and identifier-driven configuration experience
- Active-system and exact-build correlation that excludes archived, deleted, cross-workspace, stale, and mismatched releases while retaining history
- Desktop and thin-client clients, loading states, error recovery, and duplicate-action protection
- Shared UI, host integration, packaged desktop, thin-client, accessibility, and regression tests
- Updated Systems, Publish, lifecycle, operations, security, context-pack, and contributor documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish-action-progression`: An unpublished or unsupported build has no lifecycle controls; a published uninstalled build shows Install; successful Install also activates and then shows Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall; inactive stopped installations show Activate and Uninstall; running systems show Stop only; Stop restores Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall for an active installation. | local | passed (test) |
| `automatic-launch-without-open-control`: Starting a qualified visual system automatically opens its exact-release interface without displaying an Open System action, while starting a nonvisual server starts it without opening a visual surface; launch and server-start failures produce truthful recoverable UI. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `no-manual-deployment-internals`: Users never enter or select deployment ids, run ids, requested capability lists, raw secret references, or egress origins for normal Publish lifecycle actions; internal identifiers and policy-derived configuration remain application-owned. | local | passed (test) |
| `active-source-identity`: Every active published build is recognizable by system name and build version and maps to its exact immutable release, while archived, deleted, cross-workspace, stale, or mismatched sources never appear as operable lifecycle cards. | local | passed (test) |
| `run-test-removed`: Desktop and thin-client Systems navigation no longer expose a standalone Run & Test tab or the superseded multi-step workflow, and direct stale routes or calls fail safely without reviving renderer-owned authority. | local | passed (test) |
| `accessible-responsive-controls`: Lifecycle controls use the existing flat design system, fit supported widths, expose loading and status feedback, preserve keyboard and focus behavior, prevent duplicate action submission, and do not flash stale or ineligible actions during refresh. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-publish-reviewed`: Automatic launch, host surface isolation, workspace and exact-release binding, archive/delete lifecycle exclusion, idempotency, policy-derived configuration, no client authority, safe diagnostics, stop and uninstall recovery, secure rollback, and residual risks are documented and evidenced. | local | passed (review) |
| `publish-experience-gates`: Focused shared UI and host tests pass before packaged desktop and thin-client end-to-end qualification plus applicable documentation, architecture, agent-support, security, build, and full repository gates run once for the completed increment. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused shared UI tests across every lifecycle state, eligible action set, duplicate click, loading, refresh, empty, blocked, archived, deleted, stale, cross-workspace, error, and recovery path.
- Run focused desktop and thin-client client and transport tests proving identifiers remain internal and automatic launch consumes only application-issued bounded descriptors.
- Run focused navigation and static cutover checks proving Run & Test and its manual forms are absent without leaving direct-call authority.
- Run packaged desktop and thin-client end-to-end qualification for build publication, install-and-activate, automatic visual launch or nonvisual start, Stop-only running state, stop, deactivate or reactivate, stopped-state uninstall, restart recovery, and archived/deleted exclusion.
- After every planned chunk is complete, run applicable docs, architecture, agent-support, security, server/thin-client build, and npm test gates once for increment 2.

### Rollback

Remove the new Publish action controls and automatic launch integration while leaving authoritative lifecycle records intact and rendering affected builds read-only; do not restore the manual identifier workflow, stale Run & Test routes, or unsupported execution.

### Excluded

- A general operations dashboard for fleet-wide deployment management
- Manual secret, capability, egress, or policy authoring inside Publish
- Arbitrary user-authored runtime UI code before sandbox qualification
- Public URL provisioning, remote hosting, autoscaling, and external production deployment
- Changes to Compose, Manage, Models, Data, or Image Generation unrelated to Publish lifecycle integration
